_note: Authoritative curriculum registry (empty lessons are a valid production state).

RED-L2-001.title: "Unit Count Thresholds: Where Residential Ends and Commercial Begins"
RED-L2-001.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Every property gets sorted into one of two worlds the moment you count its units: 1-4, or 5+. That number decides your lender, your valuation method, and your loan type."

RED-L2-002.title: "VA Loans and Creative Financing: Options at the Residential Threshold"
RED-L2-002.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Beyond conventional mortgages, VA loans and creative financing structures give eligible buyers powerful alternative paths to acquiring 1-4 unit residential properties without routing through a bank."

GOLD-L1-001.title: "The Four Jobs Money Can Do: Make, Keep, Grow, Pass On"
GOLD-L1-001.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Introduces the Make/Keep/Grow/Pass On framework that organizes the entire GOLD track."
"Defines investing in plain terms and distinguishes it from saving and speculation."

GOLD-L1-003.title: "Why Precious Metals? An Anchor Asset Class"
GOLD-L1-003.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Introduces precious metals as the concrete anchor asset used throughout this track to teach investing principles."

GOLD-L1-004.title: "Gold vs. Silver: Two Metals, Different Roles"
GOLD-L1-004.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Compares gold and silver as investment assets and explains why both appear in the track's case study."
"Introduces dollar-cost averaging as a disciplined, emotion-resistant investing approach."
"Introduces the concept of compounding and why time is one of the most powerful forces in investing."
"Explains how much risk is appropriate depends heavily on how soon the money will be needed."
"Introduces diversification as a way of managing risk by not depending on any single asset's performance."
"Explains the basic supply and demand factors that drive gold and silver prices."
"Introduces the basic units and purity measures used in the precious metals market."

GOLD-L1-011.title: "The Difference Between Investing and Emergency Savings"
GOLD-L1-011.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Clarifies why investment money and emergency savings should be treated as separate pools with different rules."
"Explains the difference between the spot price of metal and what a buyer actually pays."
"Compares two common physical forms of precious metals and their respective tradeoffs."
"Explores the decision of whether to reinvest growth or use it, and how that choice affects compounding."
"Teaches the basics of recordkeeping for an accumulating investment position."
"Addresses the emotional challenge of watching an investment's value rise and fall, and how to manage it."

GOLD-L1-017.title: "Inflation and Why It Matters to Investors"
GOLD-L1-017.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Explains inflation in plain terms and why it's a core reason investing matters at all."

GOLD-L1-018.title: "Precious Metals as an Inflation Hedge: A Historical Perspective"
GOLD-L1-018.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Examines the historical relationship between precious metals and inflation, with appropriate nuance."

GOLD-L1-019.title: "Setting an Investment Budget You Can Afford"
GOLD-L1-019.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Teaches how to determine a sustainable amount to invest without compromising other financial needs."
"Explains why the discipline of consistent investing matters more, for most people, than picking the perfect asset."
"Explores the historical role of gold as a form of money itself, before modern currency systems."
"Explains how currency strength, especially the US dollar, tends to influence precious metals prices."
"Explores how mining supply and natural scarcity influence precious metals prices over time."
"Teaches how to interpret common precious metals market headlines and terminology as a beginner."
"Explains price volatility as a normal characteristic of precious metals investing, not a sign of something wrong."
"Introduces basic considerations for safely storing physical precious metals."
"Explains liquidity as it applies to physical precious metals, comparing it to other asset types."
"Compares precious metals to stocks, bonds, and cash at a basic conceptual level."
"Introduces the concept of correlation and how precious metals have historically related to stock market movements."
"Explains the concept of opportunity cost as it applies to allocating money toward precious metals versus other investments."
"Introduces basic awareness of counterfeit risk and authentication when buying physical precious metals."
"Introduces the concept of insuring a physical precious metals collection against loss or theft."
"Provides a practical checklist for someone making their first precious metals purchase."
"Teaches practical criteria for evaluating whether a precious metals dealer is reputable and trustworthy."
"Introduces general tax considerations for precious metals investing, with appropriate caveats about individual circumstances."

GOLD-L1-036.title: "Diversification: Where Metals Fit in a Broader Plan"
GOLD-L1-036.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Explains the practical role precious metals play within a diversified portfolio, without overstating their weight."

GOLD-L1-037.title: "Physical Metal vs. Paper Gold: A Basic Comparison"
GOLD-L1-037.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Introduces paper gold exposure (like ETFs) at a conceptual level, comparing it to physical ownership."
"Identifies common mistakes beginning precious metals investors make and how to avoid them."
"Guides students through drafting a basic, personalized plan for precious metals investing."

GOLD-L1-040.title: "Reviewing and Adjusting a Metals Plan Over Time"
GOLD-L1-040.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Explains how and when a precious metals investing plan should be honestly reviewed and potentially adjusted."

GOLD-L1-041.title: "Building a DCA Plan Step by Step"
GOLD-L1-041.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Provides a concrete, step-by-step framework for building a personal dollar-cost averaging plan."

GOLD-L1-042.title: "Case Study Reflection: The Full Arc From Age 11 to 15 and Beyond"
GOLD-L1-042.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Reflects on the complete biographical case study arc, synthesizing multiple lessons from across this track."
"Explores the concept of using precious metals as part of a multigenerational wealth strategy."

GOLD-L1-044.title: "Comparing GOLD Track Concepts to WHITE Track Investing"
GOLD-L1-044.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Connects precious metals investing concepts to the broader investing principles covered in the WHITE track."

GOLD-L1-045.title: "When Precious Metals Might Not Be the Right Fit"
GOLD-L1-045.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Provides an honest, balanced look at circumstances where precious metals investing may not suit an individual's needs."

GOLD-L1-046.title: "The Relativity of Achievement Applied to Metals Investing"
GOLD-L1-046.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Applies this curriculum's relativity-of-achievement theme to precious metals investing across different starting points."
"Teaches how to set meaningful checkpoints for a long-term, gradually accumulating investment position."

GOLD-L1-048.title: "Teaching the Next Generation: An Introduction to 'Pass On'"
GOLD-L1-048.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Introduces the fourth function of the Make/Keep/Grow/Pass On framework as a preview for future levels."

GOLD-L1-049.title: "Preparing for Level 2: What's Next in Investing"
GOLD-L1-049.author: "Waldemar M. Caban, JD MA"

metadata.summary: "Previews the topics Level 2 of the GOLD track will build toward, based on the foundation established in Level 1."
"Closes Level 1 by synthesizing the track's core throughline and reinforcing the transferability of every concept covered."
